The harbour town of Saltmere sits at the mouth of the Grey River, where the fishing fleets have anchored for three hundred years.

Its people are known for their stubbornness and their smoked eel, which merchants carry as far as the inland capital.

Every spring the town holds the Tide Fair, when the guilds race painted boats across the bay and the winners choose the next harbour master.
